title: TM Synchronization and Channel Coding—Summary of Concept and Rationale
short_title: TM Sync and Channel Coding Rationale (CCSDS 130.1-G-3)
issue: Informational Report, Issue 3 (Green Book), with Editorial Change 1 (October 2024)
organisation: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS)
status_notes: The Document Control table (PDF p. 6) lists 130.1-G-1 (June 2006) and 130.1-G-2 (November 2012) as superseded and 130.1-G-3 (June 2020) as the 'Current issue'. Editorial Change 1 (October 2024) corrects text in figures 7-9 and 7-10. The report states that it is not a Recommended Standard and that the Blue Book (reference [3], CCSDS 131.0-B-3) prevails in case of conflict (PDF p. 13).
summary:
The CCSDS Green Book that explains the concepts behind the [TM Synchronization and Channel Coding](../ccsds/tm-coding.md) Blue Book and the rationale for its choices. It is a tutorial and performance reference, not a specification. Section 2 places channel coding in the layered CCSDS telemetry model: packets go into fixed-length [TM Transfer Frames](../ccsds/tm-sdlp.md), an Attached Sync Marker precedes each frame or codeblock, and coding protects the frames. Section 3 introduces the recommended code families and the BER, WER and FER performance measures on the AWGN channel, with Shannon capacity and sphere-packing bounds for comparison.

One chapter covers each code family:

* **Convolutional codes**: the (7,1/2) code, its punctured rates (2/3, 3/4, 5/6, 7/8), Viterbi decoding, soft quantisation and truncation length.
* **Reed-Solomon codes**: the (255,223) E=16 and (255,239) E=8 codes over GF(2^8), symbol interleaving, virtual fill and shortening, and hard algebraic decoding.
* **Concatenated RS + convolutional coding**, including frame lengths for each interleaving depth.
* **Turbo codes**: the encoder, the iterative decoder, performance for rates 1/2 to 1/6, error floors and burst erasures.
* **LDPC codes**: the near-Earth C2 code and the deep-space AR4JA family, their encoders and decoders.

Chapter 9 covers the ancillary functions an implementer of a ground decoder or frame synchroniser needs: the pseudo-randomiser (h(x) = x^8+x^7+x^5+x^3+1) and its spectral problems at high data rates, frame synchronisation for each code, the CCSDS CRC-16 used as the FECF, code transparency and NRZ-L/NRZ-M conversion. Annexes give a glossary, soft-decision quantisation strategies and the rationale for the turbo-code parameters. The 72-entry bibliography is the classic coding literature behind the standard.

key_points.text: The report is informational only; in case of conflict the TM Synchronization and Channel Coding Recommended Standard (CCSDS 131.0-B-3, its reference [3]) prevails.
The TM Transfer Frame is fixed-length to ease synchronisation on weak space-ground signals and to suit block-oriented codes; an Attached Synchronization Marker signals the start of each frame.

Recommended codes: the constraint-length-7 rate-1/2 convolutional code and its punctured versions; the (255,223) and (255,239) Reed-Solomon codes and their shortenings; RS+convolutional concatenations; and families of Turbo and LDPC codes.
Code performance is reported on the AWGN channel against Eb/N0 using three measures: BER, WER (codeword error rate) and FER.
The (7,1/2) convolutional code achieves free distance dfree = 10, which no other rate-1/2 code with K <= 7 matches.
Both RS codes use the field generator polynomial F(x) = x^8+x^7+x^2+x+1; their code generator polynomials are self-reciprocal, which simplifies the encoder.
Frame lengths for RS interleaving depths I = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8 are 1784 to 14272 bits for E=16 and 1912 to 15296 bits for E=8 (Table 6-1).
Turbo-code performance is shown for rates 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 and 1/6 with information block lengths 1784, 3568, 7136 and 8920 bits (10 decoder iterations).
Two LDPC sets were chosen: a quasi-cyclic high-rate code (C2, a modified regular (4,32) code) for near-Earth links and nine AR4JA codes (rates 1/2, 2/3, 4/5; k = 1024, 4096, 16384) for deep space.

The pseudo-randomiser uses h(x) = x^8+x^7+x^5+x^3+1, repeats every 255 bits and is reset to all ones at the start of each codeblock, codeword or frame; its first 40 bits are 1111 1111 0100 1000 0000 1110 1100 0000 1001 1010.
At high data rates, the short (N = 255) standard randomiser applied to zero-filled idle frames can produce spectral spurs that break ITU power-flux-density limits, so a longer LFSR may be needed.
The CCSDS CRC-16 used for the Frame Error Control Field has generator polynomial G(X) = X^16 + X^12 + X^5 + 1.
Optional NRZ-L to NRZ-M conversion at the transmitter (and its inverse at the receiver) resolves phase ambiguity: NRZ-M represents a '1' by a change of level.

notes: The slug's 'e1' is Editorial Change 1 (October 2024); the Document Control page footer carries an extra 'October 2024' date. PDF pages 1 and 2 are duplicate cover pages. The extraction has 131 PDF pages (registry: 130). Although this is the June 2020 issue, it cites TM Synchronization and Channel Coding issue 3 (131.0-B-3, September 2017) as its reference [3], not the later 131.0-B-4 or 131.0-B-5. Many figures (performance curves, block diagrams) extract as scattered labels. Reference [15] prints 'Apri–June 1995' and [20] prints 'Inernational' (typos in the source). In references with personal authors, the authors are put in parentheses after the title; journal or report details are recorded in doc_id. Section 1.4 is a plain 'References' list, catalogued as kind 'reference'. No individual authors of the report are named.
